3. The learned subordinate Judge by referring to the argument of the defence counsel that plaintiffs became aware of the deed of exchange dated 15.4.72 from the written statement filed by defendant No.1 in C.C. Suit No. 177 of 1973 which was brought by the predecessor or the plaintiffs and by referring to a judgment of the Additional District Judge in Title Appeal No. 69 of 1975 and other documents produced by the defendant found that the suit was barred by limitation and by constructive res-judicata and on such finding rejected the plaint. 

 4. Mr. B. N. Chowdhury, the learned Advocate representing the Appellants submitted that the rejecting of the plaint on the aforesaid grounds was illegal. His contention was that a plaint can be rejected under Or. 7 r. 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure only when the plaint itself shows that the suit is barred by any law He maintained that the statement made in the plaint did not at all show or indicate that the suit was barred by any law nor the subordinate Judge could make any such finding. Contrarily the learned Subordinate Judge held the suit to be barred by limitation and by res judicata by referring to the written statement and other documents produced by the defendant and this was unauthorised by the provisions of Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 7. In this case as we have already mentioned the learned Sub-ordinate Judge found the suit to be barred by limitation and by res-judicata not at all on the basis of the statements in the plaint but on the reference of some facts in the written statement and on some documents produced by the defendant. The Subordinate Judge did not find nor Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin could show to us that anywhere in the plaint it was disclosed or indicated in any way that the suit was barred by any law. In such a position the Subordinate Judge was not authorised by the provision of Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure to reject the plaint and his assailed order is therefore untenable in law. 

 8. Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin made an alternative submission that if the rejection of the plaint is held to be illegal a direction may be made on the Subordinate Judge to frame issues on the point of limitation and res judicata and to dispose of the said issues as preliminary points It is in the domain of the trial court to frame appropriate issues on the basis of the pleadings and so we are not inclined to give direction in that regard.
